title: Too Many Losing Heroines!
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Self-described background character Kazuhiko Nukumizu, a loner who reads light novels, overhears popular classmate Anna Yanami being turned down by her childhood friend. Soon he is entangled with several 'losing heroines', including track star Lemon Yakishio and shy literature-club member Chika Komari, each rejected by the boy she loved. He helps them move on, and in the process makes real friends for the first time. A manga adaptation of a light novel set in Toyohashi; ongoing.
life_message: Heartbreak is survivable, and friendship can grow from shared loss.

content.note: Crushes and rejection; MangaDex suggestive, MangaUpdates Big Breasts (low votes).
Heartbreak, loneliness and social anxiety (Wikipedia: Chika's stutter, Nukumizu's isolation).

dominant: Recovering from rejection; friendship for a loner; gentle comedy

frames.aligns: Nukumizu's patient friendship consoles the heartbroken girls.
Humility of the 'background character' serving others.
Bearing one another's burdens after rejection.
Putting the best construction on Anna's antics.
Friendship that draws a loner into community.
Gentle comedy of manners and consolation.
Good companionship and patience in disappointment.
Letting go of attachment to a lost love.
Girls given depth and self-worth beyond romance.
Loyal friendships; respect for sister Kaju's care.
Local Toyohashi setting and sincere friendships.
Self-interest of a loner who chooses his company.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Rejections are absorbed and girls stay friends with rivals (Wikipedia: Lemon and Chihaya).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Personal feelings and choices drive the plot.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Friend group outweighs family; sister Kaju supportive.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Popular girls and a loner become equals.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Emotional fulfillment and enjoying life after heartbreak.

folkways.japan: Plays on the Japanese romcom convention of the 'make-heroine' (losing heroine) and the school club as social world.

delivery.evidence: Wikipedia notes critics praised humor and emotional depth; no review called it preachy (to verify).
delivery.note: Comedy carries a light message about recovering from rejection.

winners_losers: The heroines recover and Nukumizu gains friends; the boys who rejected them are not villains; sympathy goes to the 'losers'.
to_verify: Wikipedia and its reception cover the light novel and anime, not the manga adaptation.
Fan-service level in the manga (MangaDex suggestive).
